name: Dirty Purple
lede: Dirty Purple is a dark, grayed reddish purple named by the 2010 xkcd color survey, where it sits almost on top of a Ridgway swatch no one connected it to.

sections.title: A crowd name, close to an older one
sections.body:
The only recorded source for Dirty Purple is the xkcd survey of 2010, built on the plain modifier grammar *dirty* plus [[purple]] [1]. At hex #734A65 it measures lightness 37 and chroma 24 in LCH, and its nearest ISCC-NBS block is a dark reddish purple, 7.8 units off [1]. No earlier book or chart carries this exact name [1].

Its closest named neighbor is [[dull-dark-purple|Dull Dark Purple]], only 2.6 units away and almost the same color, a Ridgway swatch from 1912 that the two surveys never cross-referenced [2]. Further out sit [[raisin-purple|Raisin Purple]], 4.4 units off and more vivid, and [[old-lilac|Old Lilac]], 4.7 units off, purpler and brighter [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.09% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (22 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 7 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 72% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow across its 7 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1337, 673 years before the name's 2010 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
